subject.title: [Bug]: Hallucination Loop — Agent Generated Irrelevant Multi-Thousand-Word Responses Across 2 Simultaneous Sessions

question: Should this incident be treated as a supported-config outcome of shared `session.dmScope: "main"`, a Telegram/session delivery bug, or a new semantic runaway-output safety requirement?
rationale: The current source shows configured isolation and documented shared-DM defaults, while the payload-free diagnostics prove a send burst but not the exact semantic contamination path; choosing the repair boundary requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Investigate session and delivery bug first
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run live Telegram proof that separates shared-DM configuration from duplicate delivery, reconnect replay, and cross-session context drift before changing defaults.

options.title: Route as configuration/support
options.body: Treat the reporter's missing dmScope as expected shared-main behavior and close only after maintainers explicitly accept that current docs/onboarding are sufficient for multi-user Telegram bots.

options.title: Sponsor a semantic guard
options.body: Define an opt-in or default runaway-output/cancellation policy for irrelevant long responses across channels, with separate tests and product copy.

recommendation.title: Investigate session and delivery bug first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run live Telegram proof that separates shared-DM configuration from duplicate delivery, reconnect replay, and cross-session context drift before changing defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the broadest product-boundary choice among the likely owners because it crosses routing defaults, delivery reliability, and semantic guard policy.
